diagnosis.summary: The nightly run b2ef7bb4 (partition 2026-10-01) failed at quality_checks. The row_count_trend checks failed for raw.orders, raw.order_items and raw.payments, each at about 40–45% of its trailing median. Root cause: upstream sent a filtered export. Only web-channel orders were included, and the app and marketplace channels are missing entirely. The files are not truncated, and no dbt model or ingest config changed. I've proposed asking upstream to redeliver orders, order_items and payments for 2026-10-01 and then rerunning. If the redelivered files are identical to the bad ones, escalate to upstream_app_team.

root_cause.explanation: The 2026-10-01 landing export for orders has only web-channel rows (205). The app and marketplace channels, normally about 120–180 and 52–95 orders a day, have zero rows. order_items and payments contain only the matching web subset of orders. The files are structurally clean and cover all hours of the day, with order ids scattered across the full range, so the export was filtered by channel, not truncated. Ingest loaded them without errors, and the drop surfaced only as row_count_trend failures.

evidence.claim: quality_checks failed because row_count_trend failed for raw.orders, raw.order_items and raw.payments (44%, 40% and 45% of median)
Ingest succeeded with no warnings. Customers were unchanged at 30, while orders, order_items and payments each fell by about 55–60% versus 09-30
The orders export is web-only: app and marketplace are at 0 while web volume is normal
This is not a truncation: rows cover all hours, the file ends cleanly, and the gaps in order ids are scattered
order_items and payments contain the same web-only subset of orders
No dbt model changes and no ingest config changes
The runbook says to request redelivery of all three tables for a one-off filtered export, and to escalate to upstream if the resend is identical

alternatives_considered: Partial or truncated export: ruled out because rows cover all hours, the file ends cleanly, and the gaps in order ids are scattered rather than the range stopping early
Genuine business dip: unlikely, because only two channels went to exactly zero while web volume was normal
Bad dbt model deploy: ruled out because no models changed and the raw counts themselves are low

Deliberate, permanent upstream change (e.g., channels moved to another feed): possible, but there is no evidence of it. Only one day is affected. If the redelivered files are identical, escalate to upstream_app_team
rerun_only: would not help, because the landing files themselves are missing the data

proposal.rationale: The 2026-10-01 export was filtered to the web channel only. The app and marketplace channels have zero rows, while web volume is normal and the rows cover every hour of the day. order_items and payments contain only that same web subset of orders. There are no schema changes, no dbt model changes, and no ingest errors. This is a one-off filtered export. The runbook remedy is to ask upstream to redeliver orders, order_items and payments together for that day and then rerun the partition. If the redelivered files are identical to the bad ones, escalate to upstream_app_team.

applied: upstream re-exported orders (440 rows), order_items (840 rows), payments (417 rows) for 2026-10-01
